at ødelægge.explanation: "At ødelægge" means "to destroy or break". To say you broke your own phone: "Jeg ødelagde min telefon" (I broke my phone). To say a thing broke without anyone doing it, use "at gå i stykker" (to break): "Telefonen gik i stykker" (The phone broke).

sentence.da: Børnene må ikke **ødelægge** den gamle vase.
sentence.en: The children must not break the old vase.

at øge.explanation: "At øge" means "to increase". To say you make something bigger yourself, use it with the thing: "Vi øger farten" (We increase the speed). When something goes up by itself, use "at stige" (to rise): "Prisen stiger" (The price is rising).

sentence.da: Firmaet vil **øge** prisen næste år.
sentence.en: The company will increase the price next year.

at ønske.explanation: "At ønske" means "to wish". To wish someone something, put the person after the verb: "Jeg ønsker dig en god tur" (I wish you a good trip). To wish for something for yourself, add "sig" (oneself): "Jeg ønsker mig en cykel" (I wish for a bike).

sentence.da: Vi vil **ønske** hende tillykke i morgen.
sentence.en: We will wish her congratulations tomorrow.

at ønske sig.explanation: "At ønske sig" means "to wish for". To say what you want to get, use it with the thing: "Jeg ønsker mig en cykel" (I wish for a bike). To wish something to another person, leave out "sig" and use "at ønske" (to wish): "Jeg ønsker dig held og lykke" (I wish you good luck).

sentence.da: Børn plejer at **ønske sig** en hund til jul.
sentence.en: Kids usually wish for a dog for Christmas.

at øse.explanation: "At øse" means "to scoop or pour". To say you bail water out of a boat: "at øse vand ud af båden" (to bail water out of the boat). To say it is raining very hard, use it with "ned" (down): "Det øser ned!" (It is pouring down!)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **øse** suppen op i skålene.
sentence.en: I will ladle the soup into the bowls.

at øve.explanation: "At øve" means "to practice". To say you practice yourself, add "mig" (myself): "Jeg øver mig i dansk" (I am practicing Danish). To say you rehearse something, put it right after the verb: "Børnene øver en sang" (The children are rehearsing a song).

sentence.da: Hun skal **øve** sig i at spille klaver.
sentence.en: She has to practice playing the piano.

at øve sig.explanation: "At øve sig" means "to practice". To say you practice, use "mig" (myself): "Jeg øver mig hver dag" (I practice every day). To say he or she practices, use "sig" (himself, herself): "Hun øver sig på klaveret" (She practices on the piano).

sentence.da: Han skal **øve sig** i dansk hver dag.
sentence.en: He has to practice Danish every day.

en ø.explanation: "En ø" means "an island". In Denmark, Copenhagen lies on the island "Sjælland" (Zealand).

sentence.da: Vi tager færgen til en lille **ø**.
sentence.en: We take the ferry to a small island.

en øjenfarve.explanation: "En øjenfarve" means "an eye color". To ask someone's eye color: "Hvad er din øjenfarve?" (What is your eye color?) To answer: "Jeg har brune øjne" (I have brown eyes).

sentence.da: Min **øjenfarve** er grøn, og min fars er blå.
sentence.en: My eye color is green, and my father's is blue.

en øjenlæge.explanation: "En øjenlæge" means "an eye doctor". It is built from "et øje" (an eye) and "en læge" (a doctor). To get your sight tested at a shop, go to "en optiker" (an optician): "Jeg skal til optikeren" (I am going to the optician).

sentence.da: En **øjenlæge** undersøger dine øjne og dit syn.
sentence.en: An eye doctor examines your eyes and your sight.

en øjenvippe.explanation: "En øjenvippe" means "an eyelash". To describe someone's eyelashes, use the plural: "Hun har lange øjenvipper" (She has long eyelashes).

sentence.da: Hver **øjenvippe** hjælper med at holde støv ude af øjet.
sentence.en: Each eyelash helps keep dust out of the eye.

en økonom.explanation: "En økonom" means "an economist". The subject is "økonomi" (economics). For example, "Hun læser økonomi" (She studies economics).

sentence.da: En **økonom** kan forklare, hvorfor priserne stiger.
sentence.en: An economist can explain why prices rise.

en økonomi.explanation: "En økonomi" means "an economy". It also means a person's or a household's finances. For example, "Vi har en stram økonomi" (Our finances are tight).

sentence.da: Landets **økonomi** er stærk.
sentence.en: The country's economy is strong.

en økse.explanation: "En økse" means "an axe". To say you chop wood, use the verb "at hugge" (to chop): "Jeg hugger brænde" (I chop firewood).

sentence.da: Vi hugger træ med en skarp **økse**.
sentence.en: We chop wood with a sharp axe.

en øl.explanation: "En øl" means "a beer". To order a certain size, put the size word between "en" and "øl": "en stor øl" (a large beer).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker en kold **øl**.
sentence.en: I drink a cold beer.

en ølflaske.explanation: "En ølflaske" means "a beer bottle". It is built from "en øl" (a beer) and "en flaske" (a bottle). To order a bottle of beer: "En flaske øl, tak" (A bottle of beer, please).

sentence.da: Øl er i en **ølflaske**, og vin er i en vinflaske.
sentence.en: Beer is in a beer bottle, and wine is in a wine bottle.

en ønskeseddel.explanation: "En ønskeseddel" means "a wish list". It is built from "at ønske" (to wish) and "en seddel" (a note). In other words, "seddel" means a banknote. For example, "en hundredkroneseddel" (a hundred-krone banknote).

sentence.da: Hun skrev en lang **ønskeseddel** til jul.
sentence.en: She wrote a long wish list for Christmas.

en ørering.explanation: "En ørering" means "an earring". It is built from "et øre" (an ear) and "en ring" (a ring). To talk about a matching set, say "et par øreringe" (a pair of earrings).

sentence.da: Jeg har mistet min venstre **ørering**.
sentence.en: I have lost my left earring.

en ørken.explanation: "En ørken" means "a desert". To say where you are, use "i" (in) before the word: "Vi gik i ørkenen i tre dage" (We walked in the desert for three days).

sentence.da: Der er næsten ingen regn i en **ørken**.
sentence.en: There is almost no rain in a desert.

en ørn.explanation: "En ørn" means "an eagle". An eagle that lives near the sea is "en havørn" (a sea eagle). For example, "Vi så en havørn ved fjorden" (We saw a sea eagle by the fjord).

sentence.da: En **ørn** flyver højt over bjergene.
sentence.en: An eagle flies high over the mountains.

en ørred.explanation: "En ørred" means "a trout". A trout that lives in the sea is "en havørred" (a sea trout). For example, "Han fangede en havørred" (He caught a sea trout).

sentence.da: En **ørred** ligner en laks, men den er mindre.
sentence.en: A trout looks like a salmon, but it is smaller.

en øse.explanation: "En øse" means "a ladle". To say you serve food with it, use "at øse op" (to scoop out): "Han øser maden op" (He scoops out the food).

sentence.da: Han tager suppe op af gryden med en **øse**.
sentence.en: He takes soup out of the pot with a ladle.

en østers.explanation: "En østers" means "an oyster". Oysters from the fjord "Limfjorden" are called "limfjordsøsters" (Limfjord oysters).

sentence.da: En **østers** er en musling, som man ofte spiser rå.
sentence.en: An oyster is a kind of shellfish that people often eat raw.

en øvelse.explanation: "En øvelse" means "an exercise". It comes from the verb "at øve" (to practice). In sport or at the gym, it means one move of a workout. For example, "Gør denne øvelse ti gange" (Do this exercise ten times).

sentence.da: Børnene laver en **øvelse** i matematik hver dag.
sentence.en: The children do a math exercise every day.

et øje.explanation: "Et øje" means "an eye". To say you watch someone or something, use "at holde øje med" (to keep an eye on): "Jeg holder øje med børnene" (I keep an eye on the children).

sentence.da: Jeg har noget i mit **øje**.
sentence.en: I have something in my eye.

et øjeblik.explanation: "Et øjeblik" means "a moment". It is built from "et øje" (an eye) and "et blik" (a glance). To say right now, use "i øjeblikket" (at the moment): "Jeg læser i øjeblikket" (I am reading right now).

sentence.da: Vent et **øjeblik**, tak.
sentence.en: Wait a moment, please.

et øjekast.explanation: "Et øjekast" means "a glance". It is built from "et øje" (an eye) and "et kast" (a throw), so it is a throw of the eyes. To say how something seems at first glance, use "ved første øjekast" (at first glance): "Ved første øjekast er det en god pris" (At first glance it is a good price).

sentence.da: Et hurtigt **øjekast** på kortet var nok til at finde vej.
sentence.en: A quick glance at the map was enough to find the way.

et øjenbryn.explanation: "Et øjenbryn" means "an eyebrow". To say someone raises an eyebrow, use the verb "at løfte" (to lift): "Han løftede et øjenbryn" (He raised an eyebrow).

sentence.da: Han har et ar over det venstre **øjenbryn**.
sentence.en: He has a scar over his left eyebrow.

et øjenlåg.explanation: "Et øjenlåg" means "an eyelid". It is built from "et øje" (an eye) and "et låg" (a lid). In other words, "et låg" is also a lid on a pot. For example, "et låg på en gryde" (a lid on a pot).

sentence.da: Når du sover, er dine **øjenlåg** lukkede.
sentence.en: When you sleep, your eyelids are closed.

et økosystem.explanation: "Et økosystem" means "an ecosystem". It is built from "øko" (eco) and "et system" (a system). The same "øko" is in "økologisk" (organic). For example, "økologiske æg" (organic eggs).

sentence.da: Når der er for få bier, ødelægger det et helt **økosystem**.
sentence.en: When there are too few bees, it ruins a whole ecosystem.

et ønske.explanation: "Et ønske" means "a wish". To say a wish came true, use "gå i opfyldelse" (to come true): "Mit ønske gik i opfyldelse" (My wish came true). The verb is "at ønske" (to wish): "Jeg ønsker dig held og lykke" (I wish you good luck).

sentence.da: Hendes største **ønske** er en hund.
sentence.en: Her biggest wish is a dog.

et øre.explanation: "Et øre" means "an ear". It is also a small unit of money worth a hundredth of a krone. To say a price with it: "Mælken koster tre kroner og halvtreds øre" (The milk costs three kroner and fifty øre).

sentence.da: Jeg har ondt i mit **øre**.
sentence.en: My ear hurts.

øde.explanation: "Øde" means "deserted". For a place that is just calm and peaceful, use "stille" (quiet) instead: "Byen er stille" (The town is quiet).

sentence.da: Om natten er den lille by helt **øde**, og ingen er ude.
sentence.en: At night the small town is completely deserted, and nobody is out.

ødelagt.explanation: "Ødelagt" means "broken". It comes from the verb "at ødelægge" (to destroy). To say a day or a plan is ruined: "Dagen er ødelagt" (The day is ruined).

sentence.da: Min telefon er **ødelagt**, fordi jeg tabte den.
sentence.en: My phone is broken because I dropped it.

ødelæggelse.explanation: "Ødelæggelse" means "destruction". It comes from the verb "at ødelægge" (to destroy). To talk about the damage after a flood: "Oversvømmelsen efterlod store ødelæggelser" (The flood left great destruction).

sentence.da: Stormen forårsagede stor **ødelæggelse** i byen.
sentence.en: The storm caused great destruction in the town.

ødelæggende.explanation: "Ødelæggende" means "destructive". It comes from the verb "at ødelægge" (to destroy). To describe a fire that does great damage: "en ødelæggende brand" (a destructive fire).

sentence.da: Den **ødelæggende** orkan lagde mange huse i ruiner.
sentence.en: The destructive hurricane left many houses in ruins.

øjeblikkelig.explanation: "Øjeblikkelig" means "immediate". It is built from "et øjeblik" (a moment). To ask for help right away, use it before the noun: "øjeblikkelig hjælp" (immediate help). To say how someone acted, use "øjeblikkeligt" (immediately) after the verb: "Han svarede øjeblikkeligt" (He answered immediately).

sentence.da: Han fik **øjeblikkelig** hjælp, fordi det var meget alvorligt.
sentence.en: He got immediate help because it was very serious.

øjeblikkeligt.explanation: "Øjeblikkeligt" means "immediately". To say how quickly a person acts, use it after the verb: "Han svarede øjeblikkeligt" (He answered immediately). Before a noun, use "øjeblikkelig" (immediate): "øjeblikkelig hjælp" (immediate help).

sentence.da: Brandalarmen går, og alle forlader bygningen **øjeblikkeligt**.
sentence.en: The fire alarm goes off, and everyone leaves the building immediately.

øjensynligt.explanation: "Øjensynligt" means "apparently". It contains "øje" (eye) and "syn" (sight). It can also come first in the sentence. For example, "Øjensynligt er han træt" (Apparently he is tired).

sentence.da: Vinduet er åbent, så han er **øjensynligt** hjemme.
sentence.en: The window is open, so he is apparently home.

økologisk.explanation: "Økologisk" means "organic". In Denmark, organic food in shops carries the red "Ø-mærket" (the organic mark). To talk about organic eggs, use the plural ending: "økologiske æg" (organic eggs).

sentence.da: Jeg køber helst **økologisk** mælk.
sentence.en: I prefer to buy organic milk.

økonomisk.explanation: "Økonomisk" means "economic". When you describe a car that costs little to run, it means "economical": "en økonomisk bil" (an economical car).

sentence.da: Vi har brug for **økonomisk** hjælp.
sentence.en: We need financial help.

øm.explanation: "Øm" means "sore". To say a body part is sore when touched: "Min arm er øm" (My arm is sore). To say something hurts, use "at have ondt" (to hurt): "Jeg har ondt i armen" (My arm hurts).

sentence.da: Min skulder er **øm** efter træning.
sentence.en: My shoulder is sore after exercise.

ønskelig.explanation: "Ønskelig" means "desirable". It comes from the verb "at ønske" (to wish). To say it would be good if everyone comes: "Det er ønskeligt, at alle kommer" (It is desirable that everyone comes).

sentence.da: En **ønskelig** løsning er både billig og nem.
sentence.en: A desirable solution is both cheap and easy.

øreringe.explanation: "Øreringe" means "earring". It is the plural, used when you mean more than one: "Jeg køber to øreringe" (I am buying two earrings).

sentence.da: Hun har små **øreringe** i ørerne.
sentence.en: She has small earrings in her ears.

øst.explanation: "Øst" means "east". To name the eastern part of a region, put it before the name: "Østjylland" (eastern Jutland).

sentence.da: Solen står op i **øst**.
sentence.en: The sun rises in the east.

østersøen.explanation: "Østersøen" means "the Baltic Sea". The Danish island Bornholm lies in it. For example, "Bornholm ligger i Østersøen" (Bornholm lies in the Baltic Sea).

sentence.da: Færgen sejler over **Østersøen** til Polen.
sentence.en: The ferry sails across the Baltic Sea to Poland.

østpå.explanation: "Østpå" means "east". It is built from "øst" (east) and "på" (on). To say where a place lies, use "øst for" (east of) instead: "København ligger øst for Roskilde" (Copenhagen is east of Roskilde).

sentence.da: Vi tager **østpå** efter frokost.
sentence.en: We are heading east after lunch.

øvelse gør mester.explanation: "Øvelse gør mester" means "Practice makes perfect". Literally, it says that exercise makes a "mester" (master).

forms.da: Øvelse gør mester, så bliv ved
forms.en: Practice makes perfect, so keep going

sentence.da: Jeg læser højt hver dag, fordi **øvelse gør mester**.
sentence.en: I read aloud every day because practice makes perfect.

øverst.explanation: "Øverst" means "at the top". The opposite is "nederst" (at the bottom). For example, "Navnet står nederst på siden" (The name is at the bottom of the page).

forms.en: at the top of the list
at the top of the page

sentence.da: Min yndlingsbog står **øverst** på hylden.
sentence.en: My favorite book is at the top of the shelf.
